headers.description: Optional headers to send with the request as a dictionary of header values.

Content-Type.description: The media type of the resource being requested, typically 'application/json'.

Authorization.description: The credentials to authenticate a user agent with a server, typically formatted as 'Bearer {token}'.

timeout.description: The maximum amount of time to wait for a response from the server, in seconds. A longer timeout may be necessary for slower network connections or overloaded servers. This is a float type value.

params.description: URL parameters to append to the URL. Sent as a dictionary of key-value pairs.

query.description: The query parameter for search or filtering.

page.description: The page number parameter for pagination. Used to retrieve a specific page of results.

auth.description: HTTP authentication credentials formatted as a (username, password) tuple.

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem), if required for the request.

cookies.description: Cookies to send with the request as a dictionary of cookie names and values.

sessionid.description: Session identifier cookie, used to recognize client sessions on the server.

csrftoken.description: CSRF protection token cookie, used to prevent cross-site request forgery attacks.

proxies.description: Proxy settings as a dictionary, mapping protocol or protocol and hostname to the URL of the proxy.

http.description: Proxy URL to use for HTTP requests, including the port number.

https.description: Proxy URL to use for HTTPS requests, including the port number.

stream.description: Whether to stream the download of the response. If False, the response content will be immediately downloaded. Streaming is useful for handling large files or responses.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not. Set to False to skip certificate verification, which is not recommended unless you are sure of the server's identity.

message.content:
Below is a quick‑start guide for a single, well‑documented service that does exactly what you’re looking for: **ipinfo.io**.  
It accepts an IP address (or “me” for the caller’s IP) and returns a JSON payload that includes a `company` object with contact details when available.

---

## 1. Endpoint

```
GET https://ipinfo.io/<IP>/json?token=<YOUR_TOKEN>
```

* `<IP>` – the IPv4 or IPv6 address you want to look up.  
* `<YOUR_TOKEN>` – your personal API key (free tier gives ~50 k requests/month).

If you omit the token you’ll still get a limited response, but it won’t include the `company` field.

---

## 2. Sample Request (cURL)

```bash
curl "https://ipinfo.io/8.8.8.8/json?token=YOUR_TOKEN"
```

---

## 3. Sample Response

```json
{
  "ip": "8.8.8.8",
  "hostname": "dns.google",
  "city": "Mountain View",
  "region": "California",
  "country": "US",
  "loc": "37.3860,-122.0840",
  "postal": "94035",
  "timezone": "America/Los_Angeles",
  "org": "AS15169 Google LLC",
  "company": {
    "name": "Google LLC",
    "domain": "google.com",
    "phone": "+1-650-253-0000",
    "email": "support@google.com",
    "address": "1600 Amphitheatre Parkway, Mountain View, CA 94043, USA"
  }
}
```

> **Note:**  
> * The `company` field is only populated for IPs that belong to a registered organization.  
> * Some fields (e.g., `email`, `phone`) may be omitted if the provider doesn’t expose them.

---

## 4. Quick Python Example

```python
import requests

def lookup_ip(ip, token):
    url = f"https://ipinfo.io/{ip}/json"
    params = {"token": token}
    resp = requests.get(url, params=params, timeout=5)
    resp.raise_for_status()
    return resp.json()

if __name__ == "__main__":
    data = lookup_ip("8.8.8.8", "YOUR_TOKEN")
    print(data.get("company", "No company data available"))
```

---

## 5. Other Languages (snippets)

| Language | Code |
|----------|------|
| **Node.js** | ```js\nconst fetch = require('node-fetch');\nasync function lookup(ip){\n  const res = await fetch(`https://ipinfo.io/${ip}/json?token=YOUR_TOKEN`);\n  console.log(await res.json());\n}\nlookup('8.8.8.8');\n``` |
| **PHP** | ```php\n$ip = '8.8.8.8';\n$token = 'YOUR_TOKEN';\n$url = "https://ipinfo.io/{$ip}/json?token={$token}";\n$response = file_get_contents($url);\necho $response;\n``` |
| **Ruby** | ```ruby\nrequire 'net/http'\nrequire 'json'\nuri = URI('https://ipinfo.io/8.8.8.8/json?token=YOUR_TOKEN')\nres = Net::HTTP.get(uri)\nputs JSON.parse(res)['company']\n``` |
| **Go** | ```go\npackage main\nimport (\n  \"encoding/json\"\n  \"fmt\"\n  \"net/http\"\n)\nfunc main(){\n  resp, _ := http.Get(\"https://ipinfo.io/8.8.8.8/json?token=YOUR_TOKEN\")\n  defer resp.Body.Close()\n  var data map[string]interface{}\n  json.NewDecoder(resp.Body).Decode(&data)\n  fmt.Println(data[\"company\"])\n}\n``` |

*(Feel free to ask for a snippet in another language if you need one.)*

---

## 6. Free Tier Limits & Pricing

| Plan | Requests per month | Company data | Notes |
|------|--------------------|--------------|-------|
| **Free** | 50 000 | Yes (but rate‑limited) | No authentication header needed, but you’ll get a `company` field only if the IP belongs to a known org. |
| **Pro** | 1 000 000 | Yes | Requires API key, higher rate limits, more detailed data. |
| **Enterprise** | Custom | Yes | Dedicated support, custom SLAs. |

> **Tip:** For production workloads, sign up for a Pro key to avoid hitting the free tier’s 1 request/second limit.

---

## 7. Privacy & Compliance

* ipinfo.io complies with GDPR and CCPA.  
* The `company` field is only returned if the IP is registered with a business that has opted into the public database.  
* If you’re handling sensitive data, consider adding a privacy notice and ensuring you’re not storing personal data longer than necessary.

---

## 8. Alternative Services

| Service | Key Feature | Free Tier |
|---------|-------------|-----------|
| **ipapi.co** | `org` field (organization name) | 30 k requests/month |
| **ipstack.com** | `company` field (name, domain, phone) | 10 k requests/month |
| **ipgeolocation.io** | `company` + `contact` sub‑object | 20 k requests/month |

All of them follow a similar pattern: `GET https://<service>/v2/<IP>?apiKey=YOUR_KEY`.  
Pick the one that best matches your quota and pricing needs.

---

### TL;DR

Use `https://ipinfo.io/<IP>/json?token=YOUR_TOKEN`.  
It returns a `company` object with name, domain, phone, email, and address when available.  
Try the cURL example above, or drop in the Python snippet to get started right away.
